text: The realigned document is numbered 3: the folder holds the family up to v2, so the next version is v2 plus 1, and the 'Version 1' of the source metadata table is kept visible in the Source version row and in the change log instead of being carried forward as the version row.
why: Template and Rules R8.2 fixes the next version as the highest v<n> of the family plus 1, and the source filename and the source metadata table disagree on the number.
read: Source metadata table and file name; the family in 05 Technical architecture.
applied_in: Metadata table (Version, Source version rows) and Change log
confirm: The document owner aligns the metadata Version row with the file name at the next review.
impact: None on content; the version row of the realigned document reads 3.

text: rwb-document reads the case identity and the case scope through the case contract of P3 rwb-case over REST, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a contract fake, class C, so that the case match of section 2 and the scope check of section 6 have a stated interface.
why: Section 2 matches a document to a case and section 6 scopes a read to the case, while Architecture v5 slide 16 lists no rwb-case operation among the IN contracts of P5 and the Ownership Map has no consumed-operation row.
read: Source sections 2 and 6; Architecture v5 slide 16; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet.
confirm: The P5 contract story confirms the operation it consumes and the P3 contract story publishes the fake.
impact: One C dependency; the build of P5 is not blocked by P3.

text: A legal hold is recorded by P3 rwb-case through POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold, because the Ownership Map gives that operation to P3 and rwb_document has no legal-hold table; rwb-document reads the hold before it proposes an expiry and never disposes of a document under one.
why: The source puts the hold in the hub, the Ownership Map puts the operation with P3, and Architecture v5 gives retention to P5; the two readings have to be joined without inventing a table.
read: Source section 7; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints and Tables sheets; Architecture v5 slide 16.
confirm: P3 and P5 confirm the hold contract at contract review; if a hold table is needed it is added to rwb_document with its own story.
impact: The hold check is a cross-service read on the case contract; retention stays in P5.

text: e-Discovery is served by GET /documents of rwb-document with the case, type and date filters, and each document is returned with its metadata and its version list; no separate e-discovery operation is introduced.
why: Section 7 requires the answer and the Endpoints sheet holds no e-discovery row, so the requirement is met with an operation that exists rather than with an invented path.
read: Source section 7; Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet.
confirm: The legal team confirms the population filter it needs at contract review.
impact: No new operation; a filter parameter is added to an existing one.

text: The document type list, its field list and the per-case-type checklist stay rows of document_type, document_checklist_item and case_document_check in rwb_document (P5) and are read through the P5 contract; they are not moved to the reference-data contract of rwb-case (P3).
why: The R-PREC default ruling gives parameters and reference data to P3, while the Ownership Map gives these three tables to P5; the map is the owner of record for a table and the document follows it.
read: Source section 3; Rules v1 R3 default rulings and DP-07; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet.
confirm: P3 and P5 confirm the split when the reference-data contract of P3 is built.
impact: Other services read the type list from P5, not from P3.

text: JOB-12 is a 15-minute trigger that starts DocumentIntakeWorkflow on queue rwb-document, with KEDA workers scaling on the intake queue; the 'intake job' of section 2 is read that way.
why: Section 2 gives no frequency, owner or mechanism and Architecture v5 slide 44 gives all three for JOB-12.
read: Source section 2; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 44.
confirm: The scheduling design of the run carries the same row.
impact: No manual trigger; the pickup is a schedule plus workers.

text: No personal field is written to the search index of rwb_document in clear form, and every response of rwb-document is masked at its own API against the masking_rule rows of rwb-access (P4); a masked field is therefore not searchable, as section 6 requires.
why: Section 6 states both the mask and the search rule without saying where either is applied, and with one index per service the index is built in P5 while the masking rows are P4.
read: Source section 6; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet; Architecture v5 slide 14.
confirm: The security design of the run holds the same rule for every service.
impact: The index holds masked values only; a search on a personal field returns nothing.

text: An e-signature request is a row of signature_request in rwb_document (P5) and is raised through P5's activity contract on queue rwb-document by the service that needs the signature, which for a settlement agreement is S2 rwb-treatment.
why: The source names e-signature once, Architecture v5 lists signatures under P5 and the Ownership Map gives the table to P5, but no call path is stated anywhere.
read: Source section 3; Architecture v5 slides 16, 17 and 18; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet.
confirm: The P5 and S2 contract stories confirm the activity contract at contract review.
impact: One activity contract to publish; no new topic.

text: 'Blob storage' in the source is read as Azure Blob with a write-once container for legal types, holding the files as a claim-check with the file ID in the case, the workflow and the events, planned at 2.8 TB by 2031; DL27 stays open for the backup and legal-hold detail.
why: Section 1 and section 2 name the store without naming the platform and leave DL27 open, while Architecture v5 slide 16 names the store and the volume.
read: Source sections 1 and 2 and the DL27 row; Architecture v5 slide 16.
confirm: The storage decision DL27 confirms the container and the backup at the next architecture review.
impact: No file bytes travel on the bus or in a workflow input.

text: An overdue original raises its task through the task contract of P3 rwb-case and carries MSG-P5-004 on the case; the custody row itself stays in rwb_document, so the officer sees the reminder in the case worklist and not in a second queue.
why: Section 5 names 'task to document services' with no queue, and tasks and queues are P3 resources in the Ownership Map.
read: Source section 5; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet.
confirm: P3 and P5 confirm the task creation at contract review.
impact: One C dependency on the task contract of P3.

text: The document is issued as Draft. No approval is recorded for version 3, so the overlay of the D-RCV-60 run is applied and the status stays Draft until the later verification loop.
why: AGENTS.md rule 9 and the run overlay: a missing approval or status is recorded as an assumption and the work continues.
read: AGENTS.md rules 1 to 14; run overlay D-RCV-60.
confirm: The later verification loop records the approval and changes the status.
impact: The document is usable but not approved.

text: Dates are kept as the source writes them: the source date 28 October 2026 stays visible in the Source version row and the change log, this version is dated 22 November 2026, and no date is moved or raised as a gap; dates are read as tentative under U7.
why: AGENTS.md rule 10 and U7: dates are copied unchanged and every release date is read as tentative.
read: Source metadata table and header line.
confirm: Dates are confirmed at the later verification loop.
impact: No date changes; the document stays inside the 8-month programme.

text: Every owner named in version 3 is a service code of the Microservice Ownership Map v1 and _work/msr/plan/ownership.json: P5 rwb-document for the document, custody, OCR, signature and retention tables and the 17 REST operations; P3 rwb-case for the legal hold, the task and the case contract; P4 rwb-access for the masking rows and the access log; P10 rwb-agent for the classify and extract runs; S2 rwb-treatment for the settlement e-signature; S9 rwb-partner for the partner upload.
why: Template and Rules R1 U3 and R3: the owner is a service, never a team type and never a person, and the Ownership Map is the record.
read: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx.
confirm: The assembler checks the owner codes against the same map.
impact: No owner in the document is a name of a person or a team type.

text: The new decision identifiers used in version 3 are the ones allocated for the run: DL44 to DL49 from the Rules v1 R8.4 table and _work/msr/plan/ids.json, with ADR-013, ADR-014, ADR-016, ADR-019, ADR-020, ADR-022 and ADR-023 cited where the change needs them; no ADR, DL or D-RCV number is invented.
why: Rules v1 R8.4 names DL44 to DL49 and ADR-013 to ADR-023, and ids.json holds the same allocation.
confirm: Step D1 numbers the registers and keeps the same identifiers.
impact: No identifier collision; D-RCV-53 is not used.

text: The six document types and the fields extracted for each of them are copied unchanged from the source, with their retention classes and their arrival paths, because the field list is still open under DL19 and no higher source replaces it.
why: Section 3 is the document's own content and DL19 is still open; R-PREC gives no higher source for a type or a field name.
read: Source section 3; the DL19 row of section 8.
confirm: Legal and the business sign the field list under DL19.
impact: No type and no field is added or removed by the realignment.
